Molecular mechanisms of addiction · First-year biology

One pathway, six ways in

Every addictive drug raises dopamine in the nucleus accumbens. They do it by breaking into different stretches of the same pathway. Watch where each one gets in.

A common misconception. Dopamine molecules do not travel from start to finish. What travels is an electrical signal, an action potential, along the axon. Dopamine waits at the far end, packed in vesicles, and is released only when the signal arrives.
讲解提示开场先纠正一个常见误解：多巴胺分子并不从起点走到终点。沿着轴突 (axon) 跑过去的是电信号，叫动作电位 (action potential)；多巴胺一直装在终点的囊泡 (vesicle) 里，电信号一到才被释放。可以这样说："What travels is electricity. Dopamine waits at the finish line."

    About this modelshow

    Time is slowed about 4 times. The axon terminal is magnified and the axon is shortened. Dopamine levels come from a simple teaching model, tuned so that long-run levels roughly match rat microdialysis studies (Di Chiara and Imperato 1988): amphetamine-type stimulants about 10 times normal, cocaine about 3 times, nicotine and opioids about 1.5 to 2 times. High dopamine also slows the dopamine neuron (D2 autoreceptors); the model shows a mild version, and in some rat studies the slowing is much larger. "Firing" and "Brake" show each neuron's rate as a percentage of the no-drug panel.

    讲解提示推荐顺序：先看左上角"No drug"对照组，指出刹车（蓝色脉冲）和吸尘器（青色 DAT）；然后看第一行的尼古丁和阿片类，都作用在起点 ①，一个踩油门，一个松刹车；再看赌博，同样在 ①，但没有任何外来分子；最后看第二行的可卡因和冰毒，它们不会让放电变快（多出来的多巴胺反而让放电稍慢），而是改变终点：可卡因堵住回收，冰毒倒空囊泡并让 DAT 反转。可以打开顶部的 Quiz 让学生先猜。

    The Dopamine Line: a metro map

    The same pathway, drawn like a subway map. Trains are action potentials; passengers are dopamine. Pick a case on the line status board to see where it disrupts service, or click a station on the map. The map runs the same simulation as the 3D view.

    Line status

    Dopamine on the platform, compared with no drug

    How to read this map

    show
    • Pink line: the dopamine neuron, from the VTA to the nucleus accumbens
    • Yellow train: an action potential (the electrical signal)
    • Pink passengers: dopamine molecules
    • Depot: vesicles, loaded by VMAT2
    • Teal loop: recycling by DAT (reuptake)
    • Blue line and red signal: the GABA brake
    • Green line: "gas" inputs; nicotine opens its gates
    • Purple dashed line: inside the receiving neuron, where lasting changes build up
    讲解提示比喻对照：列车 = 动作电位 (action potential)；乘客 = 多巴胺 (dopamine)；车库 = 囊泡 (vesicle)，由 VMAT2 装车；站台 = 突触间隙 (synaptic cleft)；青色环线 = DAT 回收 (reuptake)；红色信号灯 = GABA 刹车；⑤ 站的闸机 = D1/D2 受体；紫色虚线 = 受体之后细胞内部的传话链（G 蛋白 → cAMP → ΔFosB）。讲法：先用 No drug 讲清楚"正常运营"，再点状态板上的每种药物，看是哪一站出了故障。站台上的乘客越多，多巴胺越高。可以这样说："Every drug disrupts a different station, but they all crowd the same platform."

    The dopamine machine

    Pick a case. In the guided story the machine first runs normally while each part is introduced; then the drug arrives and you see exactly which part it tampers with. In “Before & after” the same machine runs twice, side by side: without the drug and with it. Click any part of the story picture to read about it.

    Before: no drug

    After

    Live readings vs. no drug · they move up and down, like real neurons Rotor speed (firing)100% Brake presses (GABA)100% Dopamine in the gap100%

    How to read this picture

    show
    • Rotor: the dopamine neuron. It turns on its own; each hammer tap on the contact is one action potential
    • White glove: glutamate. A hard push makes a burst of taps
    • Blue operator: a GABA neuron. He steps on the seesaw brake: its red pad presses the hub. Opioids put him to sleep (zZ); alcohol and THC make him drowsy (z)
    • Rockets (nicotine cases): nicotinic receptors on the rotor arms. Nicotine is the key that lights them
    • Blue-white sparks on the cable: electricity along the axon, not dopamine
    • Warehouse and factory: one axon terminal; the faint copies are thousands more. The factory makes dopamine; the little gumball machines riding the conveyor belt are vesicles, each refilled through its cyan lid (VMAT2); a pulse opens the gate under the belt and the package over it empties all at once
    • Gate and teal RECYCLE pumps: release into the gap, and recycling by DAT, which pulls dopamine back to be packed again
    • Pink marbles: dopamine molecules (not to scale: a real package holds thousands). They spread out at random (they do not fall); some happen to land in receptors, the cups on top of the receiving cells
    • D1 scale (go): receptor cups on its pan and a heavy weight on the other arm; only many full cups at once sink the pan onto the go pedal
    • D2 scale (stop): receptor cups on its pan and the stop boot on the other arm; a few full cups keep the boot lifted, a dip lets it stamp. Each scale presses its pedal through a spring; the pedals send signals along the cells’ output fibers (green and red lines) to the BEHAVIOR dial, whose needle swings between DO IT AGAIN, no change and HOLD BACK for the action just taken (for example, the next cigarette)
    讲解提示使用方法：先选"No drug"，让学生跟着字幕看完一遍正常运转（转轮 → 电线 → 仓库和工厂 → 传送带闸门和回收泵 → 两台天平和踏板）；再依次选每种药物：第一次会完整导览，之后每种药物先放 5 秒正常运转回顾，再演示药物到达、哪里被改变、结果，最后是长期变化（一次用药不等于成瘾）。想直接看药物，可以点步骤条上的"2"。点画面上任何一个部件，下面会显示这一站的说明。切换到"Before & after"，左右两台同样的机器同时运转：左边不用药，右边用药，圈出的是药物作用的部位；下方表格汇总所有药物。可以这样说："Same machine every time. Watch which part each drug tampers with."

    English definitions follow the rest of this page. Translations were prepared for teaching; standard scientific terms were preferred over literal ones.

    Takeaways

    Same finish line

    Every case ends the same way: more dopamine reaching receptors in the nucleus accumbens. Drugs that do not do this rarely cause addiction (Nestler 2025).

    Two kinds of doors

    Station 1 cases (nicotine, opioids, gambling) change how often the dopamine neuron fires. Station 3 and 4 cases act at the terminal: cocaine keeps released dopamine around longer, and methamphetamine pushes dopamine out even when the neuron is quiet (Lüscher and Ungless 2006; for gambling, Fiorillo et al. 2003).

    Lasting changes

    With repeated drug use, the receiving neurons at station 5 change: ΔFosB builds up and switches genes on and off for weeks, and brain scans of people with addiction show fewer D2 receptors. The dopamine neuron at station 1 changes too. These changes help explain why craving can last for months after the drug is gone. Tolerance is different: it fades during a break, so taking an old dose after a break can cause an overdose.

    Treatments use the same doors

    Naloxone pushes opioids off μ-opioid receptors; varenicline partly occupies nicotinic receptors. "Virtually all available treatments for drug addiction act on the initial protein targets" (Nestler and Lüscher 2019).

    Think it through. A medicine called tetrabenazine blocks VMAT2. Imagine it does nothing else. Would dopamine in the synapse go up or down? Use the stations to explain.
    讲解提示答案：会下降。VMAT2 被堵住，多巴胺装不进囊泡（第 ③ 站），留在细胞质里的多巴胺会被 MAO 分解，电信号到达时能释放的多巴胺就少了很多。丁苯那嗪 (tetrabenazine) 正是用这个原理治疗亨廷顿病的不自主运动。可以追问：冰毒也干扰 VMAT2，为什么多巴胺反而上升？因为冰毒还让 DAT 反转，把细胞质里的多巴胺泵出去。这道题检验学生是否理解"每一站各管什么"。
